evidence.summary: In-memory USERS dict keyed by email; each record holds id, salt, hash and role 'user'.
register() lowercases the email, makes a 16-byte random salt, hashes with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 at 100,000 iterations, sets role 'user' and id len(USERS)+1; an existing email is silently overwritten.
login() looks the email up lowercased and raises ValueError('bad credentials') for both an unknown email and a wrong password; the hash comparison uses != (not constant-time).
A successful login creates a token with secrets.token_urlsafe(24) and stores SESSIONS[token] = user id; there is no logout, expiry or lookup function.

architecture.backend: single Python module with in-memory dicts; no web layer

features.name: Register with email and password
features.description: Create an account from an email address and a password.
features.observed_behaviour: register(email, password) lowercases the email, salts and hashes the password with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 (100,000 iterations, 16-byte salt) and stores the account with role 'user' and an integer id. Returns nothing.
features.business_logic: Email is case-insensitive (lowercased). Role is always 'user'. Id is len(USERS)+1. No password rules. Registering an email that already exists replaces the existing account (a takeover flaw).
features.integration: Needs the unified user store and the role model.

features.name: Log in with email and password
features.description: Sign in with email and password and get a session token.
features.observed_behaviour: login(email, password) re-hashes the password with the stored salt; on a match it returns a new random token and records it in SESSIONS; otherwise raises ValueError('bad credentials').
features.business_logic: Same error for unknown email and wrong password. Comparison is not constant-time. Sessions never expire and cannot be revoked; there is no logout or token lookup.
features.integration: Needs a unified session store with logout and lookup.

entities.name: User
entities.description: A person who signs in with email and password

entities.name: Session
entities.description: An opaque login token mapped to a user id

auth.session: opaque bearer token in an in-memory store, no expiry

error_handling.behaviour: raises ValueError('bad credentials'), same message for both
no error; the existing account is overwritten

unknowns: What the 'user' role is allowed to do: Passbook has no permission checks (role is stored, never read).
Whether overwriting an existing account on re-registration is intended; treated as a flaw to fix.
